svg.title: The DMCN trust model: mailbox users, domain operators and fleet operators
svg.text: Three kinds of actor, each holding its own keys. Every link between them is signed, and the recipient's
app checks each one back to a DNS anchor.
key never held on a server
No anchor of its own. The
Fleets need no trust between them
Mail goes straight to the recipient's
relay, signed with the sender's key.
Each side checks the other domain's DNS.
Optional onion routing adds relay hops
first; each can unwrap only one layer.
Has keys made on their own devices, never on a server.
Holds the only keys that open their mail.
Can retire their own address without the operator.
Owns the domain's DNS and an offline root key.
Can vouch for, revoke or reassign its addresses.
Cannot decrypt mail or sign with a user's key.
Runs relays and bridges under an offline root key.
Can delay or drop the mail it carries.
Cannot read it, alter it, or forge an address.
The only keys on servers belong to relays, bridges and the issuers that sign new addresses day to day, and each carries only the narrow powers its credential grants.
One organisation can be both domain and fleet operator by running its own relays. The roles stay separate in the protocol, and no domain can speak for another.
